## ✨ Added

- **Files backup domain (#62).** A fourth first-class domain alongside containers, VMs and the flash drive, with its own **Files** tab. Add named **file sets** (a label plus a host folder such as a cache or array share), each with its own restic exclude patterns. Full parity with the other domains: schedules, retention, off-site replication, integrity and disaster-recovery drills, dashboard protection card and heatmap, notifications and the Storage card. Restore a file set in place after an explicit confirmation, or into a folder you choose. Sources must be visible under the container's `/mnt` mapping, which the Unraid template's default Host Data mount already covers. A file set cannot be renamed once it has backups (its snapshots are tagged by name), so pick the name up front or create a new set.
- **Restore from another BombVault repo (#61).** A new card on the Recovery page opens another BombVault instance's backup repository, using that instance's `APP_KEY`, as a one-time read-only session. Browse its containers, VMs and file sets and restore any of them onto this server. The session lives only in memory and expires by itself, nothing is ever written to the other repository, and your own backup settings stay untouched. Mount the other server's backup share and point the card at it. (Live server-to-server federation is out of scope.)
- **Off-site verification on the dashboard (#63).** The off-site integrity drill, the only off-site proof VMs can carry, now shows its own "off-site verified" badge on each domain's protection card, next to the local-verify and disaster-recovery badges.

- **Start, end and duration for every backup run.** The dashboard Run History now shows each run's start → end and total runtime, not just the latest backup per container, but the full timing in one list. Each container and VM also gets a **Recent runs** list under its Backups section. (#50)

- **Update after successful backup (per container).** Turn it on for a container (Advanced, off by default) and BombVault pulls the image and recreates it after a successful backup, but **only when a newer image is available**, so it never needlessly restarts something that's already current. The fresh backup is your safety net, and each update shows as its own **Update** entry in the Run History. Works for scheduled and manual backups. (#52)

- **Summarise scheduled runs** (Settings → Notifications). A scheduled run of many containers/VMs used to send one message per item on every channel, so 45 containers meant 45 emails. BombVault can now send a single "N of M succeeded" summary per run instead. Healthchecks was already summarised; this brings the message channels (webhook, Matrix, email, ntfy, Unraid) in line. Off by default, and manual backups still notify per item. (#56)
- **Notify on container update.** When "update after backup" upgrades a container to a newer image, BombVault can send a message per updated container so you can verify it still works. It fires only on a real update (rare) and is separate from the scheduled-run summary. Off by default. (#56)
- **Remove the old image after an update** (Settings → Storage → Image cleanup). After a post-backup update, optionally delete the superseded image. Off by default. Keeping it makes rolling back cheap (a BombVault snapshot restores your data, not the old image), and a base image shared by other containers is never deleted. (#56)

Thanks to @BaukeZwart (#56).

- **Container healthcheck** (#60, thanks @BaukeZwart). The image now ships a Docker `HEALTHCHECK`: BombVault probes its own `/api/health` and reports the container as healthy or unhealthy, so an auto-heal tool (Autoheal and the like) can restart it if the engine ever wedges. It runs the binary itself, so nothing extra is added to the image.

## 🎨 Design

- **Local snapshot retention moved to Paths & Storage.** It used to sit under the Off-site tab; it now has its own **Snapshot retention** card next to the backup paths it prunes. Off-site retention stays on the Off-site tab. (#51)
- **Last Backups and Run History are separate dashboard blocks.** Hit **Customize** to hide either one, so Run History can then use the full width for easier reading. (#50)

- **The dashboard's Customize control is now a pencil icon in the top-right corner** instead of a text button; the Reset button and hint appear while you're editing.
- **Clearer Unraid notifications setup.** They run over the SSH connection from *VM Backup over SSH* but do **not** need libvirt or VMs; the hint says so now, and that VM SSH "Test connection" makes clear the SSH link itself is fine when only libvirt is missing. Use **Send test** on the Notifications tab to check notifications. (#53)

Thanks to @strese and @BaukeZwart.

- **The off-site DR check button reads "Re-run" once a check has passed** (shown by the green "proven off-site" badge), so it is clearly an optional re-check rather than a pending task.

## ⚡ Improved

- The heatmap, per-domain Healthchecks and the Storage card all cover the new files domain.
- Default repository layout is now `/mnt/user/bombvault/{container,vms,flash,config,files}`.
- Existing installs migrate automatically; the new domain and the foreign-restore card are opt-in and off until you enable them.

- **The Docker template mounts `/mnt` as rslave (Read/Write - Slave).** So a remote share that mounts after the container starts becomes visible to BombVault without a restart. Existing installs: re-apply the template from Community Apps, or set the **Host Data** mount's Access Mode to **Read/Write - Slave**, to get the no-restart recovery. (#55)

- **Disaster-recovery definitions now live inside each repo** (container definitions in `<repo>/def`, VM definitions in `<repo>/vm-def`) instead of separate `bombvault-defs` / `bombvault-vm-defs` folders. This keeps the backup root clean and makes a copy of a repo folder self-contained. Definitions in the old location migrate into the repo automatically on the next backup, and a restore from an older backup still finds them via a fallback.

## 🐛 Fixed

- **Failed container backups are now visible (#64).** When a whole-batch fault (a lost repo mount, a full disk, a restic error) hit some containers, those failures were not recorded, so the dashboard showed nothing and the notification was a bare "N failed". Every container failure is now recorded with its reason, shows up in the run history and heatmap, and the scheduled notification names which containers failed and why.

- **The "What's new" dialog finds its notes on `:latest` builds.** `:latest` images carry a version like `vX.Y.Z+main.<sha>`; the dialog now looks up the plain release tag, so it loads, and no longer re-appears on every `:latest` rebuild, only once per real release. (#48)

Thanks to @ptmorris1 and @manilx.

- **The "What's new" dialog shows the changelog again.** It fetched the notes from GitHub at runtime, which BombVault's own Content-Security-Policy (`connect-src 'self'`) blocks, so it always fell back to an error. BombVault now serves its own release notes locally (embedded in the app), so the dialog works offline and without GitHub rate limits. The "View on GitHub" link is still there. (#54)
- **A backup share that mounts late at boot no longer looks like your backups are gone.** If BombVault started before a remote backup share (e.g. under `/mnt/remotes`) was mounted, the list showed no local backups and a new backup could fail or, worse, write an empty repo over the mount point. BombVault now recognises an established repo whose backing store has vanished, refuses to re-initialise over it (no empty-repo shadowing), and shows a clear "backup path not mounted yet" message instead of "no backups". (#55)

Thanks to @BaukeZwart (#54) and @manilx (#55).

- **Your backup folder stays readable for an off-box copy.** BombVault runs as root and restic writes each local repo owner-only (dirs `0700`, files `0600`), which on an SMB-shared backup folder could lock a non-root user out of the whole folder. After every backup BombVault now relaxes the local repo tree to group/other readable (dirs `0755`, files `0644`, only the entries that need it, setgid preserved). The repos are encrypted, so nothing is exposed, and a folder an older version locked down is healed on the next backup.

## Notes

- A file set cannot be renamed once it has backups (its snapshots are tagged by name), so pick the name up front or create a new set.

*Also includes what was previously released separately as 5.1.0, 5.2.0, 5.3.0, 5.4.0, 5.5.0.*
